faq.q: When is the F1 Grand Prix 2037 in Marbella?
faq.a: The F1 Grand Prix 2037 takes place from 6 to 8 June 2037, with practice on Friday, qualifying on Saturday, and the main race on Sunday. Yacht charters are available all weekend, and we recommend booking your boat at least 3–4 months in advance.

faq.q: How far is the circuit from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Puerto Banús is located approximately 5–10 minutes by boat from the F1 circuit area. Most of our charters depart directly from the marina, so you can watch the race from a prime offshore position without the crowds.

faq.q: Can I watch the entire race from the yacht?
faq.a: Yes, you can view the race from the sea. The coastal track layout offers excellent sightlines from the water. Our yachts anchor at a safe distance, and many guests watch from the flybridge or sundeck. We also provide binoculars and a live radio commentary feed.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). The Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. The Mangusta 80 costs €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours and includes a jet ski.

faq.q: Which boats are best for a group of 10–12 people?
faq.a: For groups of 10–12, we recommend the Azimut 58 Flybridge (12 pax), Mangusta 80 (12 pax), Ferretti 94 (12 pax), or Canados 86 (12 pax). These yachts have spacious decks, flybridges, and ample seating for race-day viewing. Pricing for these boats is available on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can I book a yacht for just the race day (Sunday)?
faq.a: Absolutely. Sunday charters are our most popular for the F1 weekend. You can book a half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours) charter. For example, the Tier A boats start at €749 for 2 hours, but we recommend at least a 4-hour slot to enjoy the race and the after-party atmosphere.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on race day?
faq.a: We monitor weather forecasts closely. In case of adverse conditions (strong winds, thunderstorms), we may postpone or cancel the charter with a full refund or reschedule option. The skipper makes the final call for safety. Marbella generally enjoys calm seas in June, with average temperatures of 26–30°C.

faq.q: How do I book an F1 Grand Prix yacht charter?
faq.a: You can book directly through our website or contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing on our larger yachts. We recommend booking as early as possible – for the 2037 race, many boats are reserved by March. A 50% deposit secures your slot, with the balance due 14 days before departure.

data.body_html:
The F1 Grand Prix 2037 is set to be one of the most spectacular events on the Costa del Sol. And there’s no better way to experience it than from the deck of a private yacht, anchored just off the coast. Our boat rental Marbella service offers a fleet of luxury vessels departing from Puerto Banús, putting you right at the heart of the action. Whether you want to watch qualifying from a flybridge or celebrate the podium with champagne on a sundeck, we’ve got the perfect boat for your weekend.

The race weekend runs from 6–8 June 2037, with practice on Friday, qualifying on Saturday, and the main race on Sunday. All our charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA – no hidden fees. Below, we break down the best boats, pricing, and what to expect.

Why charter a yacht for the F1 Grand Prix in Marbella?

Watching the Grand Prix from a yacht offers three major advantages: unobstructed views, total privacy, and a party atmosphere. From the water, you can see the track’s coastal sections without the crowds, noise, or queues. You control the music, the food, and the guest list. Plus, Puerto Banús is just minutes from the circuit, so you can dock, grab a bite at a chiringuito, and be back on board before the next session starts.

Marbella’s June weather is near-perfect – average sea temperature of 22°C, air temperatures hitting 30°C, and gentle breezes. The combination of F1 adrenaline and Mediterranean luxury is hard to beat.

Our F1 Grand Prix 2037 fleet

We have 16 boats available for the 2037 weekend, ranging from compact speedboats to superyachts. All depart from Puerto Banús. Here are the standout options for race-day viewing:

For smaller groups, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are nimble options. The Bandido (11.5m, 8 pax) offers a good middle ground. Pricing for these is on request via WhatsApp.

What’s included in every charter

All our charters include: licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). That means you don’t pay extra for the skipper, fuel, or taxes. The Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are priced at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. The Mangusta 80 (both white and grey) costs €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours and includes a jet ski – perfect for buzzing around the bay between sessions.

For larger yachts like the Azimut 58 Flybridge, Ferretti 94, or Canados 86, pricing is available on request. We’ll tailor a quote based on your preferred duration and any extras (catering upgrades, additional hours, water toys).

Sample F1 weekend itinerary

Here’s a typical Sunday race-day plan on a Mangusta 80:

  • 10:00 – Board at Puerto Banús. Meet your skipper, stow bags, enjoy welcome cava.
  • 10:30 – Depart marina. Cruise along the coast to the best anchor point near the circuit.
  • 11:00 – Anchor up. Snacks and drinks served. Set up binoculars and radio feed.
  • 13:00 – Race start. Watch from flybridge or aft deck. Jet ski available for a spin.
  • 15:00 – Post-race celebration. More cava, music, and a swim off the stern.
  • 17:00 – Return to Puerto Banús. Disembark or extend into the evening.

You can adapt this to your group’s pace – some guests prefer a shorter 4-hour charter, others make a full day of it with lunch at a beach club en route.

How to book your F1 Grand Prix yacht charter

Booking is straightforward. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) and the Mangusta 80, you can book directly on our site. For all other yachts, contact us via WhatsApp for availability and a personalised quote. We recommend booking at least 3–4 months in advance – for the 2037 race, many boats are fully reserved by March. A 50% deposit secures your slot, with the balance due 14 days before departure.

If you’re planning a full weekend, consider a Friday practice charter (€749/2h) plus a Sunday race charter. Or book a single long charter that covers both qualifying and the race. We’ll help you choose the best combination.
